'''Puran poli''' or '''vedhmi''' is a sweet version of stuffed [[Cookbook:Chapati|chapati]] from the Gujarat in the Indian subcontinent. It is mainly stuffed with [[Cookbook:Pigeon Pea|toor dal]], but some people use [[Cookbook:Chickpea|chana dal]].

==Ingredients==
*½ [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]] [[Cookbook:Pigeon Pea|toor]] [[Cookbook:Dal|dal]]
*[[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Cardamom|cardamom]] powder
*½ kg [[Cookbook:Jaggery|jaggery]]
*½ kg wheat [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]] (maida)
*100 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] [[Cookbook:Oil and Fat|oil]]
*1 tsp [[Cookbook:Clarified Butter|ghee]]

== Procedure ==
#Wash and [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] the toor dal with water and ½ tsp salt until soft.
#Cool slightly and strain the dal using a [[Cookbook:Sieve|strainer]].
#Add cardamom powder and jaggery to the dal, then grind to make a fine paste. If the paste is sticky, keep it on the heat to dry up completely. This is known as "puran".
#[[Cookbook:Kneading|Knead]] flour with ½ tsp salt and enough water to make a [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]]. Do not make the dough hard.
#Add oil, and knead the dough again until the oil is absorbed.
#Prepare an equal number of balls from the dough and puran.
#[[Cookbook:Dough#Rolling|Roll out]] dough balls to make small un-cooked chapati.
#Stuff each uncooked chapati with a ball of puran.
#Roll them again into stuffed chapati just like stuffed paratha. It is called "poli".
#Heat a griddle and fry each poli.
#[[Cookbook:Brush|Brush]] ghee on both sides when done.
#Serve.
